subject: Microbiology
vignette: A 63-year-old man is brought to clinic by his wife because of 4 months of rapidly progressive memory loss, personality change, and unsteady gait. His wife reports sudden jerking movements of his arms that occur mostly when he is startled. He worked for many years as a shepherd and ate traditional meat products. MRI shows cortical ribboning, and CSF is positive for 14-3-3 protein. He dies 5 months after symptom onset.
question: Which of the following best describes the molecular event responsible for this patient's disease?

options.text: Alpha-helical prion protein converts to a beta-pleated, protease-resistant form
Prion protein gene mutation causing complete absence of the normal cellular prion protein
Expansion of a CAG trinucleotide repeat within the huntingtin gene
Accumulation of amyloid-beta peptide derived from cleavage of the amyloid precursor protein
Hyperphosphorylation of tau protein leading to intracellular neurofibrillary tangles

explanation_correct: This is sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, the classic prion disease: rapidly progressive dementia with ataxia and startle myoclonus, with death usually within months to a year. Prion disease results from conversion of the normal predominantly alpha-helical prion protein (PrPc) into a beta-pleated form (PrPsc); PrPsc resists protease degradation and templates the conversion of more PrPc, producing spongiform encephalopathy. Accumulated PrPsc is the transmissible agent, which is why CNS tissue and BSE-contaminated food can transmit disease.

explanation_incorrect.B: Prion disease reflects gain of a toxic, transmissible PrPsc conformation, not loss of PrPc; the normal protein is converted, not deleted, and the disease is transmissible.
explanation_incorrect.C: CAG repeat expansion in the huntingtin gene causes Huntington disease, which presents with chorea, psychiatric change, and autosomal dominant inheritance, not a rapidly progressive dementia with myoclonus.
explanation_incorrect.D: Amyloid-beta accumulation with plaques is the hallmark of Alzheimer disease, which evolves over years with an insidious amnestic onset rather than the subacute course and startle myoclonus seen here.
explanation_incorrect.E: Tau hyperphosphorylation and neurofibrillary tangles are seen in Alzheimer disease and other tauopathies, not in prion disease, which is defined by PrPsc deposition and spongiform change.

educationalObjective: Prion disease is caused by conversion of normal alpha-helical PrPc to protease-resistant beta-pleated PrPsc, producing spongiform encephalopathy with rapidly progressive dementia, ataxia, and startle myoclonus.

subject: Microbiology
vignette: A 22-year-old man in a remote highland community develops progressive ataxia, tremors, and emotional lability over several months, followed by dementia and death within a year. Epidemiological study of his community finds that the disease occurs almost exclusively among members of a group that, until recently, practiced ritual endocannibalism as part of mourning ceremonies.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Kuru is the acquired prion disease described in tribal populations that practiced human cannibalism; CNS-related tissue is the vehicle of transmission, and the illness is a cerebellar-predominant spongiform encephalopathy with ataxia, tremor, and progressive dementia. It is one of the classic three prion diseases in First Aid alongside sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease and bovine spongiform encephalopathy.

explanation_incorrect.B: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy is caused by JC polyomavirus reactivation in immunosuppressed patients and produces focal white matter demyelination rather than a transmissible spongiform process.
explanation_incorrect.C: Variant CJD is acquired from food contaminated by BSE-infected animal products, so it is linked to beef consumption and mad cow disease, not to ritual cannibalism.
explanation_incorrect.D: Bovine spongiform encephalopathy is the prion disease of cattle, also called mad cow disease; it is the animal source that can transmit variant CJD to humans rather than a human illness.
explanation_incorrect.E: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis follows measles infection years earlier in childhood and shows myoclonic jerks with EEG periodic complexes, not a dietary-ritual epidemiological pattern.

educationalObjective: Kuru is the acquired human prion disease associated with ritual cannibalism; prion transmission requires CNS-related tissue or BSE-contaminated food.

subject: Microbiology
vignette: A hospital sterilizing services unit is revising its protocols after a patient with confirmed Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease underwent a brain biopsy. The surgical instruments were processed with the standard autoclave cycle used for all other surgical trays. The infection control committee asks whether that cycle was adequate and what distinguishes the prion agent from conventional pathogens.
question: Which of the following statements about the prion agent is most accurate?

options.text: A protein conformation that resists standard autoclaving
It is a bacterium that lacks a cell wall and therefore resists beta-lactam antibiotics
It is a self-replicating nucleic acid that is destroyed by protease digestion
It is a fungus that is killed by ethylene oxide but survives pressurized steam
It is an RNA virus that is inactivated by standard autoclaving but not by alcohols

explanation_correct: PrPsc is a misfolded protein conformation, and it resists protease degradation and standard sterilizing procedures including standard autoclaving, which is why prion-contaminated instruments require special decontamination protocols. Its resistance to proteases is itself part of the diagnostic concept: PrPsc survives proteinase K digestion while normal PrPc does not. The transmissible agent is the abnormal protein itself, not a nucleic acid genome.

explanation_incorrect.B: Prions are not bacteria; the absence of a cell wall describes Mycoplasma and does not explain protease resistance or autoclave resistance.
explanation_incorrect.C: No self-replicating nucleic acid has been identified in prions; the infectious entity is protease-resistant protein, so protease digestion does not destroy infectivity.
explanation_incorrect.D: Prions are not fungi. Fungi are killed by pressurized steam, whereas the prion protein is the entity that survives standard autoclaving.
explanation_incorrect.E: Prions are not viruses and contain no RNA genome; standard autoclaving is exactly the procedure that may fail to reliably inactivate them.

educationalObjective: PrPsc is a protease-resistant protein conformation that survives standard sterilizing procedures, including standard autoclaving.
